title: Add human verification gate to ticket-do command
story: As a developer, I want the ticket-do command to pause and ask me to verify before closing a ticket, so that I always have a chance to review changes before a ticket is marked done.
acceptance_criteria: ticket-do always pauses and asks the user for confirmation before closing a ticket
The agent waits for explicit user confirmation before closing
non_goals: Automatically determining which tickets need more scrutiny
Presenting a structured testing checklist (vs. a simple confirmation prompt)
Blocking closure if tests are failing (separate from human sign-off)
Logging or recording the sign-off confirmation
assumptions: The user is present and available to respond when ticket-do reaches the sign-off step
ticket-do is always run interactively (not in a batch or unattended mode)
The user will genuinely review changes before confirming, not rubber-stamp

title: Add plan re-confirmation step on plan changes in ticket-do
story: As a developer, I want the agent to re-confirm the updated plan with me whenever the plan changes mid-execution, so that I always have visibility and approval before implementation continues.
acceptance_criteria: ticket-do instructs the agent to re-present the full updated plan whenever a change is made mid-execution
The agent waits for explicit user confirmation before continuing after a plan change
The re-confirmation step is identical in form to the initial plan confirmation step

title: Replace LLM-driven verbatim field entry in ticket-do with explicit instruction
story: As a developer, I want verbatim text I provide to be placed into ticket fields exactly as given, without the agent interpreting or acting on it, so that data entry is reliable.
acceptance_criteria: ticket-do explicitly instructs the agent to treat user-provided verbatim text as inert data to be transcribed, not as instructions to act on
The agent asks for confirmation before taking any action when the user is in the middle of providing field values

title: Local script to retrieve next ticket number
story: As a developer, I want a local script that retrieves the next ticket number so that I don't contribute towards LLM API usage limits.

title: Script to record user retro feedback verbatim
story: As a developer, I want a script to record my retro feedback directly into the ticket JSON so that the LLM cannot interpret or act on it.
acceptance_criteria: A script exists that accepts a ticket ID and prompts for user_retro text via stdin
The script writes the input verbatim to the user_retro field of the matching ticket in current-sprint.json
The retro command instructs the agent to invoke this script for collecting user_retro rather than asking in chat

title: add more single-word object words and move word generation into a script and out of the readme
story: as a developer, i want a script to generate high quality prompts for object writing exercises
acceptance_criteria: A script or skill exists that generates one- or two-word object writing prompts
The script's generation prompt draws on examples from Pat Pattison books
non_goals: Generating prompts longer than two words
Replacing the existing static word list
Automating prompt generation on a schedule
Building a UI for prompt generation
assumptions: Pat Pattison book examples are available to reference (the developer has access to the books)
The script is run manually on demand, not as part of the app runtime

title: Capture execution log in ticket-do for retro input
story: As a developer, I want ticket-do to record structured notes during execution so that retro feedback is based on a complete record rather than recall.
acceptance_criteria: Tickets have a `retro_notes` field with `agent` and `user` keys, each an array of strings; `agent_retro` and `user_retro` fields are no longer populated

ticket-do instructs the agent to append a plain-string note to `retro_notes.agent` at the point of occurrence for: scope increases, missing or invalidated assumptions, changed ACs, plan deviations, surprises, and blockers

`retro_notes.agent` entries are limited to retro-relevant events (problems, scope increases, missing or invalidated assumptions, changed ACs, plan deviations, surprises, and blockers) — execution steps, tool calls, and raw agent output are not recorded
The retro skill reads from `retro_notes.agent` and writes user feedback to `retro_notes.user`, replacing its prior use of `agent_retro` and `user_retro`
non_goals: Migrating or backfilling `agent_retro`/`user_retro` data from existing tickets
assumptions: The ticket schema supports adding new fields (i.e., `retro_notes` can be added without a migration script)
The agent executing ticket-do is capable of writing to the ticket JSON mid-execution

title: Carry forward unresolved problems across retros
story: As a developer, I want retros to validate whether problems raised in previous sprints have been resolved before checking for new retro issues, so that recurring problems are surfaced and managed distinctly rather than rediscovered
acceptance_criteria: Before reviewing current sprint tickets, the retro presents each problem identified in the previous retro and asks the developer whether it has been resolved.
Problems confirmed as unresolved are carried into the current retro's problem list and labeled as recurring.
If no previous retro exists, the validation step is skipped and the retro proceeds directly to reviewing current sprint tickets.
The retro reads previously raised problems from the most recent retro summary file (`tickets/retros/sprint-{N}-retro.md`) under the 'Problems Identified' section.
Recurring problems are distinguishable from newly identified problems throughout the retro, including in the five whys discussion and written summary.
Unresolved problems remain visible in subsequent retros until explicitly confirmed as resolved.
The retro summary written at the end lists which carried-forward problems were confirmed resolved and which remain unresolved.
Each recurring problem tracks how many consecutive sprints it has been carried forward; this count is displayed when the problem is presented during the validation step.
non_goals: Automatically detecting whether a problem was resolved (without asking the developer)
Migrating existing retro summary files to a new format to support sprint counts
Triggering automated actions (e.g., escalation, alerts) on long-running recurring problems
Resolving problems automatically based on whether related tickets were closed
assumptions: Previous retro summaries follow a consistent, parseable format with a 'Problems Identified' section.
Sprint numbers are sequential so the skill can reliably identify the immediately preceding retro file.
The developer is available interactively to confirm resolution of each carried-forward problem.

title: Route behavioral fixes to the relevant skill during retro
story: As a developer, I want the retro skill to prompt me to update the relevant skill directly when a behavioral problem is identified, so that the fix takes effect immediately rather than becoming a ticket that may never be actioned.

title: As a developer, i want my agents to be able to get the current iso timestamp for including in ticket fields like groomed_at
acceptance_criteria: there is a skill or script that agents can run to determine the current iso-format timestamp
agents have access to the skill or script when they would need it to populate relevant fields in tickets
